title: scripts/ is excluded from lint and typecheck, so release tooling has no static analysis
description:
scripts/ is excluded from BOTH lint and typecheck, so every .mjs in it -- including release tooling that only executes during a release -- ships with zero static analysis.

MEASURED, not inferred:
  biome.json   files.includes = ["src/**/*.ts", "test/**/*.ts", "benchmark/**/*.ts", "*.json"]
  tsconfig.json  include       = ["src/**/*.ts", "test/**/*.ts", "benchmark/**/*.ts", "*.ts"]

Neither pattern matches scripts/. `bun run lint` reports only its one pre-existing src/ warning; `bun run typecheck` never opens the directory.

PROOF IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The LCLI-481 provenance gate (scripts/release-provenance.mjs, 560 lines) shipped a completely unused top-level ANNOTATION constant and CI was green. tsconfig already sets noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters to true -- both would have caught it had the file been in scope. Found by adversarial review, not by any gate.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN RECORD rather than part of LCLI-481: the gap is a property of the repository, not of that gate. Folded into LCLI-481 it would disappear when LCLI-481 closes, which is precisely how the next person rediscovers it. Orchestrator ruling, 2026-09-13. It must NOT gate the 0.6.2 release.

THE SHARP EDGE: this is the least-inspected code in the repository and it is also the code that runs during the one irreversible operation. scripts/ holds publish-release.sh (the manual publish path that 0.6.1 shipped through and 0.6.2 will), and release-provenance.mjs. A typo in either surfaces mid-release.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE HERE: whether the whole directory can be brought in at once or whether some files need scoped exclusions, and whether benchmark/ and any other top-level directory have the same hole.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/**/*.mjs is covered by `bun run lint` (biome files.includes) and by `bun run typecheck` (tsconfig include), or any file that cannot be is excluded EXPLICITLY with a recorded reason rather than by the pattern silently missing it

The regression that proved the gap is caught: re-introducing an unused top-level constant in a scripts/ .mjs fails one of the two checks (noUnusedLocals is already enabled, so this should follow from the include alone -- verify it rather than assume it)
Any other top-level directory with the same hole is either brought in or named as deliberately excluded, so the answer is recorded rather than rediscovered
`bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` all pass, with no new warnings beyond the known pre-existing src/commands/agents.ts:216

comments.body:
IMPLEMENTATION WARNING, from the agent that caused this finding, 2026-09-13. The two halves of this task have very different costs and should probably be split.

BIOME HALF -- cheap, and it catches the exact defect that produced this record. Biome lints .mjs with no type information and no annotations required. Verified against a scratch file with biome 2.4.12:
    sample.mjs:1:7 lint/correctness/noUnusedVariables  This variable ANNOTATION is unused.
That is the dead constant that shipped green. Do this half first; it is nearly free.

TSC HALF -- NOT what AC#0 literally says, and the literal reading is a NO-OP. Adding scripts/**/*.mjs to tsconfig.json include WITHOUT allowJs does nothing whatsoever. Measured:
    error TS18003: No inputs were found in config file. Specified include paths were ["scripts/**/*.mjs"]
With --allowJs --checkJs it does check the file, and then demands JSDoc throughout: TS7006 on every untyped parameter, TS2339 on every property of a parsed JSON body (which is {} under strict). That applies to EVERY .mjs in scripts/, not just the one that prompted this.

So the honest shape is: biome now, tsc as a deliberate decision about whether release tooling is worth annotating. AC#0 as written implies both are the same edit. They are not. Re-read it before implementing rather than discovering this halfway.

NOTHING WAS CHANGED to learn this: the scratch tsconfig was created and deleted inside one command, and the biome sample lives outside the repo. biome.json and tsconfig.json are untouched on every branch.

finalSummary:
DELIVERED in PR #52, CI run 34871397731 on that PR's own head (a750c54c), all ten jobs green.
scripts/, bin/ and root *.ts are now covered by both static-analysis gates.

THE REGRESSION THAT PROVED THE GAP IS CAUGHT BY BOTH, verified by planting it again through
the exact command CI runs rather than an equivalent:

    clean            bun run lint -> 0     bun run typecheck -> 0
    unused constant  bun run lint -> 1     bun run typecheck -> 2
                     (noUnusedVariables)   (TS6133)

noUnusedVariables was PROMOTED TO "error" because it already REPORTED the planted constant
while exiting 0 -- a gate that notices and passes. That is the same absent-signal-read-as-a-
passing-one shape this repo keeps hitting, and AC#2 only required one of the two gates to
fail, so this goes past the criterion deliberately.

WHY A SECOND TSCONFIG rather than new globs on the first. Type-checking untyped .mjs/.cjs
needs allowJs + checkJs, and under the main config's `strict` that produced 25 noImplicitAny
errors -- pure noise on plain JS with no JSDoc, which would have had to be suppressed
wholesale and would have buried the nine real findings underneath. tsconfig.scripts.json
relaxes noImplicitAny there only, keeping what actually bites on untyped code
(noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, strictNullChecks) and weakening nothing for src/, test/
or benchmark/. The reasoning is in that file's header, where the next person will look.

NINE GENUINE TYPE FINDINGS FIXED, NOT SUPPRESSED: unguarded registry JSON shapes in
release-provenance.mjs (three sites), `catch (err)` on unknown in bin/lore.cjs (two), and a
`packages: []` that inferred never[] so every push was an error. Each carries a JSDoc
annotation saying why the type is what it is.

ONE FINDING LOOKED LIKE A REAL BUG AND WAS NOT, recorded because it nearly went out as one.
tsc flagged `results.some((r) => Boolean(r.commit))` in the provenance gate's propagation
grace. Had `commit` never been on the returned shape, anyAttested would be permanently false
and PASS 2 would never run -- a gate silently skipping its own retry. Reading checkOne shows
`commit` IS present on the later return arms and absent only on the early ones, where absent
correctly means "not attested". A union-typing complaint, not a defect. Checking before
announcing is the whole lesson.

A REAL CI-ONLY FAILURE, and the useful part is how it was fixed. `"types": ["node", "bun"]`
typechecked locally and failed CI with TS2688 "Cannot find type definition file for 'node'":
@types/node is in this working tree but is NOT a declared dependency, so naming it explicitly
made the config depend on an installation accident. Fixed by inheriting ["bun"] from the base
config. Verified by SIMULATING CI -- node_modules/@types/node moved aside, typecheck still
exits 0 -- because a local pass proves nothing when the local tree is exactly what made the
broken version look fine.

AC#3, COVERAGE OF EVERY TOP-LEVEL DIRECTORY, is recorded in tsconfig.scripts.json's header
rather than only here, so it survives this task closing:

    src/, test/, benchmark/   .ts       tsconfig.json + biome.json (unchanged)
    scripts/                  .mjs      tsconfig.scripts.json + biome.json  [NEW]
    bin/                      .cjs      tsconfig.scripts.json + biome.json  [NEW, SHIPS]
    playwright.config.ts      root .ts  was typechecked, now linted too     [NEW]
    docker/ evals/ npm/ patches/ research/ skills/ archive/
                                        no .ts/.js/.mjs/.cjs tracked at all

SHELL IS A NAMED, DELIBERATE GAP, not an oversight, and is filed rather than waved at. Four
tracked .sh files have no static analysis and neither biome nor tsc can give them any.
shellcheck 0.11.0 at -S warning finds 31 issues: 29 SC2034 "appears unused" in
docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh, 1 SC2148 in steps.sh, 0 elsewhere. Several of the 29 look like
CAPTURED BASELINES THAT ARE NEVER COMPARED -- LCLI298_AGENTS_BASELINE_HASH,
CODEX_BRIDGE_HASH_BEFORE/AFTER, BEFORE_INDEX/AFTER_INDEX -- which would mean assertions that
do not assert, inside a job that is one of only THREE required checks on dev. That needs
per-finding triage and a different tool in CI, so it is LCLI-490, created here with the
measurements attached and an explicit instruction NOT to bulk-suppress SC2034.
publish-release.sh itself is now shellcheck-clean; its single SC2088 was a false positive (a
display label, never used as a path) and carries a disable directive giving that reason.

bin/lore.cjs SHIPS TO USERS and this changed it: three non-interpolating template literals
became double-quoted strings, plus two JSDoc comments. Runtime-identical, but it does mean
the next release's root tarball differs from 0.6.2's. Flagged in the PR so nobody diffs the
tarball later and wonders.

bun run lint 0, bun run typecheck 0, 2983 tests pass / 0 fail, lore check 77 files 0 errors
0 warnings, with no new warnings beyond the known pre-existing src/commands/agents.ts:216.
